summary: I sent the scripted prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, made a `ratelimit` branch in place and asked two rounds of questions. It then implemented and reviewed all six tasks with subagents, running the 4-minute short soak in the foreground and the 12-minute long soak as a tracked background job. It ran the final whole-branch review and `sdd-state finish`, which saved a receipt, then asked how to finish. After I answered "merge back to main locally", it fast-forwarded main to e6576b7. The agent never went idle mid-plan without a question, so I never sent "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the session log, the screen and git state. The skill loaded first and all six tasks plus the final review were dispatched. sdd-state finish saved a receipt, and main holds the merged work. Neither soak test file was touched. Every stop was a real question, which I answered from the allowed list, and the agent never sat idle mid-plan without asking.

observations.description: On startup Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available' dialog (pinned Opus 5, latest Opus 5.5), even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No' to avoid a restart, and the session header then showed 'Opus 5.5'. This is a confusing extra prompt in an automated launch. The workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs also both default to 'No, exit'.

The agent asked the user to choose a workspace even though it had just loaded using-git-worktrees. When I said 'use whatever the skill recommends', it picked a new branch in place rather than an isolated worktree.

The agent asked a decision-records tooling question: design.md has no '## Decisions' list, so the decision-record tooling rejects it. The plan doesn't raise this, so the user gets an internal-tooling question before Task 1.

Two commit subjects have a stray trailer: 'e700e9a feat: add token bucket limiter Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' and '50b9a62 feat: add simulate command line Co-Authored-By: ...'. Implementer subagents put the trailer on the subject line instead of in the body. The final review spotted it but called it harmless.
No .gitignore, so ratelimit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ show up as untracked after the merge. plan.md:560 still says '1.5 seconds' even though the constant is 1.0. The agent pointed out both.
The Codex plugin isn't installed, so all the Codex reviews were skipped and logged as degraded gates. The agent reported this openly.

From prompt to finish-step report took about 32 minutes ('Churned for 32m 4s'). Most of that was the 4-minute and 12-minute soak tests. Per its own note, the agent re-ran the short soak itself before review even though the implementer subagent had already run it.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen right after the prompt: 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'. This came before any 'Implement Task N' Agent dispatch.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: Session log Agent descriptions include 'Implement Task 1: package and clocks' through 'Implement Task 6: integration test' and 'Final review (opus a1fb9add855a499f1): Ready to merge — 0 Critical, 0 Important'. The log also shows 'Final whole-branch code review'. `git branch` shows '* main' and `git log` shows main at 'e6576b7 test: add registry and sliding window integration test', with commits for all 6 tasks. Agent: 'I merged ratelimit into main. It went in as a fast-forward... All 27 unit tests pass'.

`git log --oneline -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returned only 'e50b4b0 initial: design, plan and soak tests'. `git diff <root> HEAD --stat` on both files was empty. `git status --short` showed only the __pycache__ dirs.

STOP: 'Before starting Task 1, I need your decision on two conflicts: the default window value (1.0s in code vs 1.5s stated in Task 5, though tests pass either way), and how to handle design.md for decision-record tooling — move/reformat it with a Decisions list (needs your approval) or skip decision notes entirely.' | question
STOP: 'Which option?' | question
(The third stop came after `sdd-state finish` had published its receipt but before the merge. I never had to send 'continue'.)
